web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: At $339.85, what long-term cash-flow growth rate is the market pricing into UnitedHealth Group, and why does the valuation multiple sit well below its 10-year average?

epigraph.quote: A low price-to-earnings ratio does not protect capital when earnings quality, regulatory rates, and price trend all deteriorate together.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: UnitedHealth Group closed at $339.85 on November 20, 2026 (TradingView: $339.88). That price gives UNH a market capitalization of $304.54 billion on 896.0 million shares [7, 29]. The stock trades at 19.40x trailing GAAP P/E ($17.52 TTM EPS) and 14.50x forward P/E. It also sits at 13.34x trailing P/FCF, 3.10x book value ($109.48/sh), and a 2.67% trailing yield [37]. That dividend runs at $9.28 annualized after the November 4 declaration of $2.32 per share [37]. Overall, these multiples sit 25% to 35% below UNH's 2016–2023 norm of 18.0x to 23.0x forward earnings [2, 26]. The market is applying a clear risk discount, and cash-flow math shows why buyers stepped back during a -16.67% weekly drop.

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: What $339.85 Implies About Future Cash Flows

web_blocks.html: Enterprise Value-to-EBITDA models distort health insurers because statutory cash backs unpaid claims. About $24.6 billion of UNH's $25.8 billion cash and $60.8 billion of bonds sit inside regulated subsidiaries backing $39.35 billion of medical costs payable [29]. Only $1.2 billion of unrestricted cash sat at the parent level on September 30, 2026 against $74.33 billion of total debt [29]. We therefore model UNH directly via Levered Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE). Starting from $22.83 billion of TTM FCF, we deduct $1.77 billion of 9M 2026 reserve releases ($1,440 million prior-year plus $331 million loss-contract) and a ~$2.06 billion net receivables factoring-timing normalization ($1.5 billion unremitted under the $2.2 billion facility plus a ~$0.56 billion working-capital timing cushion, distinct from the $5.9 billion cumulative gross 9M receivables sold) [2, 4, 29]. That bridge ($22.83B − $1.77B − $2.06B) yields a normalized Year-0 FCFE base of $19.00 billion ($21.21 per share).

We start from a baseline 9.5% cost of equity (5.04% 10-year Treasury yield plus a 4.46% regulatory and credit risk premium) and 3.0% terminal growth. Under those baseline inputs, the $304.54 billion equity value implies a 10-year FCFE CAGR of 3.15% (exact implied rate: 3.151%). At 3.0% annual FCFE compounding, fair value equals $336.02 per share. Years 1–10 supply 45.8% of total value, while terminal value supplies 54.2%. A 3.15% hurdle looks modest against UNH's 10.3% historical revenue growth [2, 26]. Yet three Negative credit outlooks, Q3 Optum Health's 3.2% margin deceleration, DOJ FCA litigation, and March 2026 IRS NOPAs require an explicit credit and settlement haircut [29].

web_blocks.the_number: $365.00 per share 12-month risk-adjusted base intrinsic value. The probability-weighted expected value sits at $352.00 per share (+3.6% vs. CMP).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We built a 10-year Levered FCFE DCF at 3.0% terminal growth. Unadjusted 5.3% CAGR at 9.5% Ke yields $399.35. Applying a +50 bps credit-outlook premium (Ke = 10.0%, $369.72) and deducting $4.0B ($4.46/sh) for DOJ/IRS settlement risk yields $365.26 (~$365.00), matching 16.0x cautious FY27E EPS of $22.80 ($364.80).
web_blocks.the_inputs: Year-0 normalized FCFE is $19.00B on 896.0M shares ($22.83B TTM FCF minus $1.77B 9M26 reserve releases minus ~$2.06B net factoring-timing normalization, distinct from $5.9B cumulative gross 9M receivables sold). Optum Health recovers cautiously from Q3's 3.2% (4.3% 9M26) toward 3.5%–4.0%.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear case is $265.00 (30% weight: 2.0% CAGR at 10.5% Ke less $4.46/sh legal hit = $266.51, or 0.0% CAGR at 9.5% Ke less $4.46/sh = $264.27). Base is $365.00 (50% weight). Bull is $450.00 (20% weight: 7.5% CAGR across 9.5%–10.0% Ke = $471.33 to $435.21, ~18.4x $24.50 EPS).
web_blocks.if_off: Each 100 bps rise in cost of equity (from 9.5% to 10.5%) cuts unadjusted 5.3% CAGR value by 13.8% to $344.07 (~$339.61 net of $4.46/sh legal reserve). A $4.0B DOJ/IRS settlement hits equity by $4.46 per share and risks buyback suspension.

web_blocks.title: Peer Valuation Matrix: UNH vs. Managed Care & Health Care Leaders

web_blocks.html: We compare UNH against managed-care insurers (ELV, CI, HUM) and healthcare leaders (MCK, LLY, ABBV). Every major commercial and Medicare Advantage payer—UNH, ELV, and CI—sits in Stage 4 below falling averages. By contrast, biopharma and drug-distribution leaders (LLY, ABBV, MCK) hold Stage 2 uptrends. Institutional buyers are penalizing underwriting opacity across all payers rather than singling out UNH alone.

web_blocks.takeaway: UNH leads managed-care peers in ROE (16.4%) and operating margin (5.3%) ahead of ELV (11.6% ROE), CI (14.1% ROE), and HUM (6.7% ROE). Yet all three Stage 4 payers lag Stage 2 biopharma leaders LLY and ABBV.

web_blocks.title: Historical Multiple Bands & Why Cheap Multiples Fail Without a Base

web_blocks.html: From 2016 through 2023, UNH traded between 18.0x and 23.0x forward earnings [2, 13]. Quarterly medical care ratios stayed tight within 20 to 40 bps of guidance back then. After the 2024 cyberattack, the 2025 V28 squeeze, and Q3 2026 IRS and credit disclosures, that multiple floor shifted lower [24, 29]. A 14.50x forward P/E looks cheap against history. Still, value traps punish buyers who step in before earnings estimates and price action stabilize.

web_blocks.html: UNH carries a risk-adjusted base value of $365.00 (+7.4%) and a probability-weighted expected value of $352.00 (+3.6%). A +3.6% 12-month expected return sits below the ~4.76% 2-year Treasury yield while exposing holders to a -22.0% bear drawdown. The multi-timeframe price structure next shows why technical and fundamental risk math agree.

book_paragraphs: Valuation starts with one clean question: what story is the current stock price already telling? At the November 20, 2026 close of $339.85, UnitedHealth Group carries a market capitalization of $304.54 billion on 896.0 million shares. That valuation puts the stock at 19.40 times trailing GAAP earnings, 14.50 times forward consensus earnings, 13.34 times trailing free cash flow, and 3.10 times book value, alongside a 2.67 percent trailing dividend yield. For nearly a decade prior to 2024, investors routinely paid 18 to 23 times forward earnings for UnitedHealth Group because its medical care ratio stayed remarkably steady and management beat guidance almost like clockwork. Today's 14.50 times forward multiple represents a structural derating of roughly 30 percent from that historical norm.

Before calling any stock cheap, an analyst must test whether the balance sheet and accounting structure allow a conventional valuation shortcut. Standard enterprise-value-to-EBITDA screens break down on health insurers because $24.6 billion of UNH's $25.8 billion cash and $60.8 billion of investment securities sit inside regulated insurance subsidiaries to back $39.35 billion in unpaid medical claims. Only $1.2 billion of unrestricted cash sat at the parent holding company on September 30, 2026, facing $74.33 billion in consolidated debt. For that reason, valuing UNH directly through Levered Free Cash Flow to Equity gives a far cleaner picture of what common shareholders actually own.

Our Reverse DCF starts with $19.00 billion of normalized annual free cash flow to equity, or $21.21 per share. Although trailing twelve-month free cash flow reached $22.83 billion, we deduct $1.77 billion of favorable 9M 2026 prior-year and loss-contract reserve releases plus a roughly $2.06 billion net receivables factoring-timing normalization—reflecting $1.5 billion unremitted under the $2.2 billion facility plus a $0.56 billion working-capital cushion, distinct from the $5.9 billion in cumulative gross nine-month receivables sold. Subtracting $1.77 billion and $2.06 billion from $22.83 billion reconciles cleanly to $19.00 billion as an honest cash-flow baseline. Discounted at a 9.5 percent baseline cost of equity with 3.0 percent terminal growth, the $339.85 share price implies 3.15 percent annual free-cash-flow growth over the next decade.

book_subsections.title: Why the Market Discounts a 3.15 Percent Growth Implied Price
paragraphs: On the surface, clearing a 3.15 percent ten-year cash-flow growth hurdle looks easy for an enterprise that compounded revenue at 10.3 percent annually over the previous decade. Yet institutional markets rarely hand out steep discounts without concrete reasons. Here, three distinct overhangs explain why buyers stepped away during the November 2026 selloff. First, management's own Q3 2026 Form 10-Q warns that CMS's finalized 2.48 percent Medicare Advantage rate update for calendar year 2027 still trails expected forward medical cost inflation, while No Surprises Act arbitration continues to push commercial out-of-network costs higher.

Second, earnings quality remains under debate. In the first nine months of 2026, UNH's reported medical care ratio improved 180 basis points year-over-year to 86.3 percent, but $1.44 billion of prior-year reserve releases and $331 million of loss-contract releases supplied roughly 68 basis points of that improvement. Moreover, Optum Health's operating margin cooled sequentially to 3.2 percent in Q3 2026 against a 4.3 percent nine-month average. Third, tail liabilities keep expanding in the footnotes: $133.35 billion of goodwill and net intangibles against $104.13 billion of equity, Negative credit outlooks from Moody's, S&P, and Fitch, unresolved DOJ False Claims Act litigation, and March 2026 IRS transfer-pricing Notices of Proposed Adjustment covering 2017 through 2020.

book_subsections.title: Three-Scenario Intrinsic Value & Sensitivity
paragraphs: To avoid anchoring on an unadjusted point estimate, we build our three 12-month scenarios explicitly from the $19.00 billion normalized FCFE DCF and then price in credit and legal realities. On an unadjusted basis at a 9.5 percent cost of equity, a 5.3 percent ten-year FCFE growth path yields $399.35 per share ($474.91 at 8.5 percent Ke and $344.07 at 10.5 percent Ke). However, Moody's, S&P, and Fitch all hold Negative outlooks on $74.33 billion of debt with only $1.2 billion of unrestricted parent cash, while Optum Health exited Q3 2026 at a 3.2 percent operating margin rather than 4 to 5 percent. Applying a 50-basis-point credit premium (10.0 percent Ke, yielding $369.72) and deducting a probability-weighted $4.0 billion ($4.46 per share) DOJ and IRS settlement reserve produces our risk-adjusted Base Case target of $365.26, rounded to $365.00 (+7.4 percent)—matching 16.0 times cautious FY2027 earnings of $22.80 per share.

In the Bear Case, weighted at 30 percent probability, elevated senior outpatient utilization pushes the 2027 medical care ratio toward 89.5 to 90.0 percent, or a $3 billion to $5 billion DOJ or IRS settlement forces management to pause share repurchases. Modeling 2.0 percent FCFE growth at 10.5 percent Ke ($270.97) minus the $4.46 per-share legal hit yields $266.51 (and zero growth at 9.5 percent Ke minus $4.46 yields $264.27), anchoring our $265.00 Bear target (-22.0 percent) near the $255.97 52-week low and roughly 12.9 times $20.50 stressed earnings. In the Bull Case, weighted at 20 percent, clean legal resolution and Optum Health recovery toward 5.5 to 6.0 percent margins drive 7.5 percent FCFE compounding ($471.33 at 9.5 percent Ke and $435.21 at 10.0 percent Ke), supporting a $450.00 target (+32.4 percent) at 18.4 times $24.50 earnings.

Weighting those three paths (30 percent Bear at $265.00, 50 percent Base at $365.00, and 20 percent Bull at $450.00) yields a 12-month expected value of $352.00 per share, or just +3.6 percent above the $339.85 close—below the ~4.76 percent yield on two-year U.S. Treasuries. Sensitivity analysis confirms how little margin of safety remains: if credit downgrades push cost of equity up 100 basis points to 10.5 percent, even 5.3 percent unadjusted cash-flow growth values UNH at $344.07 (and $339.61 after the $4.46 per-share legal reserve). Meanwhile, peer comparisons confirm that managed-care weakness is sector-wide: Elevance Health and Cigna also sit in Stage 4 downtrends, whereas Eli Lilly, AbbVie, and McKesson retain Stage 2 institutional sponsorship.

book_subsections.title: Why Value Traps Happen in Insurance & Managed Care
paragraphs: Managed-care stocks punish buyers who rely solely on trailing multiples during a downward earnings-revision cycle. Because health insurers collect premiums upfront and settle claims months later, accounting earnings can look temporarily resilient while medical cost trends quietly accelerate underneath. When prior-year reserve releases fade, reported medical care ratios step higher all at once, compressing both forward earnings estimates and the valuation multiple simultaneously. In UnitedHealth Group's case, book value per share of $109.48 implies a 3.10 times price-to-book ratio, yet $133.35 billion of goodwill and net intangibles leave tangible book value deeply negative by nearly $29 billion.

That balance-sheet reality changes how a prudent owner interprets share buybacks. While the board expanded its repurchase authorization by up to 50 million shares in November 2026, Moody's A2, S&P's A+, and Fitch's A ratings all carry Negative outlooks against $74.33 billion of consolidated debt and $4.8 billion of unconsolidated put/call obligations. Until free cash flow steadily reduces debt-to-capital toward 40.0 percent without relying on receivables factoring or statutory subsidiary dividends, aggressive buybacks cannot force a multiple re-rating back to 20 times earnings. Patient buyers wait for the balance sheet and price chart to confirm stability together.

book_subsections.title: Reconciling Segment Sum-of-the-Parts Against Consolidated Risk
paragraphs: A sum-of-the-parts view illustrates both UNH's latent value and why it remains locked today. In isolation, Optum Insight's 22.6 percent operating margin and $32 billion backlog resemble an enterprise healthcare software franchise, while Optum Rx's $114 billion nine-month pharmacy scale generates durable fee flow despite its upcoming 2028 rebate transition. Yet Note 9 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reveals that 60.3 percent of Optum's revenue comes directly from affiliated UnitedHealthcare contracts. Because the two halves share underwriting, regulatory, and Medicare Advantage exposure rather than acting as independent businesses, assigning a standalone software multiple to Optum while UnitedHealthcare battles CMS rate compression and DOJ scrutiny overstates near-term realizable equity value.

Until Optum Health moves back above 4 percent operating margins without prior-year reserve releases and credit outlooks stabilize, a blended 15.0 to 16.5 times forward earnings ceiling on cautious normalized cash flows offers a disciplined anchor. That framework keeps our risk-adjusted base fair value at $365.00 and prevents overpaying for historical reputation.

book_callouts.title: Why Financial-Services Cash Requires a Parent-Cash Adjustment
book_callouts.text: When analyzing an integrated health insurer, consolidated cash on the balance sheet is mostly statutory reserve money held inside state-regulated subsidiaries to pay future hospital claims. Only the $1.2 billion at the parent level is freely deployable for debt service, dividends, or buybacks without regulatory dividend approval, which makes rating-agency outlooks far more binding than headline cash balances suggest.
